lesson.title: Pupils' data needs care
lesson.subtitle: Personal data, four safe habits, and share the task, not the child

video.title: Pupils' data needs care
video.format_note: Animated explainer, 16:9, flat Darsi colours on paper-grey backgrounds. Narration in the lesson language; captions as separate files, never burned in.
cast: Ms Amina Bello — primary teacher, Nigeria (cameo)
Narrator — the Darsi voice (warm, peer to peer)

chapters.label: Share the task, not the child

scenes.visual: Icon cards: Parents' group; Names and all; A child laughed at. Dr Farah beside it.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: A teacher posted her class's test results in the parents' WhatsApp group, names and all. She meant well. By evening, one child's mark was a joke in the whole street.

scenes.visual: Paper-grey title card: the Darsi mark, the course name and the lesson title with the Data engineering track chip.
scenes.animation: Mark scales in with a small overshoot; the title slides up.
scenes.narration: Today: why pupils' data needs care, and the simple habits that protect it.

scenes.visual: Rows of icon and text: Name, photo, phone, mark; Sensitive: health, religion, family; Children: the most care.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Personal data is anything about a person who can be identified: a name, a photo, a phone number, a mark. Some of it is sensitive: health, disability, religion, family troubles. And children's data needs the most care of all.

scenes.visual: Icon cards joined by arrows: Shared once; Forwarded again; Stays for years.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Why so careful? Because data travels, and it stays. A list shared once can be forwarded forever. And a child can't choose what adults post about them.

scenes.visual: Numbered steps: Only what you need, for a purpose; Only the right people see it; Locked: PIN, cupboard key; Deleted when not needed.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Four habits keep it safe. Collect only what you need, for a clear purpose. Let only the right people see it. Keep it locked: a phone PIN, a cupboard key. And delete it when it's no longer needed.

scenes.visual: Rows of icon and text: Files in a locked cupboard; Not everyone has the key; Your phone: the same rules.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.on_screen_text: Like the files in the cupboard
scenes.narration: Think of the pupil files in the office cupboard. Not everyone gets the key, and the files don't go home in a teacher's bag. Treat the data on your phone the same way.

scenes.visual: Two columns: “In the group” (The class average; Groups by number) and “In private” (Each child's mark; Photos: ask first).
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.on_screen_text: Share the task, not the child
scenes.narration: Share the task, not the child. Post the class average, or groups by pupil number. Tell each family their own child's mark privately. And ask before you take or share a photo.

scenes.visual: Quiz card: the question with its answer options.
scenes.animation: Answer cards drop in one by one.
scenes.on_screen_text: What can go in the group?
scenes.narration: Quick check! I want the parents' group to know how the test went. Which of these can I post there?

scenes.visual: Icon cards: Class average: the group; Each mark: in private.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: The class average: it says how the class did, without pointing at any child. Each family then hears their own child's mark from you, in private.

scenes.visual: Rows of icon and text: Her school; Her birthday; Her route home; Together: a map to her.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Small facts add up. A pupil's school, then her birthday, then her route home: each harmless alone, together a map to the child. In a well-known study, birth date, sex and postcode alone picked out eighty-seven people in a hundred in the United States.

scenes.visual: Icon cards: Kenya, 2019; Nigeria, 2023; Egypt, 2020; South Africa: POPIA.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: The law agrees. Kenya, Nigeria, Egypt and South Africa all have data protection laws, and they ask the same things: a purpose, consent, care, and extra care for children.

scenes.visual: Icon cards joined by arrows: Read as a stranger; Choose who sees it; Nothing useful left.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: In the app, Lina, fourteen, has six public posts that each look harmless. Read them as a stranger would, then choose who sees each post. Can you leave the stranger knowing nothing useful?

scenes.visual: Quiz card: the question with its answer options.
scenes.animation: Answer cards drop in one by one.
scenes.narration: Your turn. A school trip form asks for each pupil's religion, home address, phone and blood group. What should I do?

scenes.visual: Summary card: Children's data: the most care; Only what you need; Locked, and deleted on time; Share the task, not the child. Takeaway bar: If you wouldn't pin it on the school gate, don't post it.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Ask only what the trip needs: an emergency contact and health needs, kept with care. Remember: children's data needs the most care. Collect only what you need, and lock it. And share the task, not the child.

scenes.visual: Rows of icon and text: Groups with data cards; Fine to share; Share with care; Keep private. Dr Farah beside it.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Try it in class tomorrow: play “Fine, care or private” with your pupils. Give each group cards: favourite food, class, home address, phone number, a photo, a test mark. They sort them into three piles, and say who may see each one.

checkpoints.prompt: The parents' group should hear how the test went. Which can you post there?

options.text: The class average for the test
A list of the pupils who failed

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — the average tells parents how the class did without pointing at any child. Each mark goes to its own family, privately.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — a list with names, or of those who failed, points at children. Post the class average, and give each family its child's mark privately.

checkpoints.prompt: A trip form asks for each pupil's religion, home address, phone and blood group. What should you do?

options.text: Collect it all, just in case
Ask only what the trip needs: an emergency contact and health needs
Post the form in the class WhatsApp group

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — the trip needs a way to reach a parent and to know about health needs. Religion and the home address aren't needed.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — collect only what the trip needs, for its purpose: an emergency contact and health needs, kept with care.
